elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The access and use rights granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI." Since "Company" is defined only as The Deerskin Companies, Inc., this is new, non-duplicative coverage.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 1.4 as rendered nor the inserted sentence mentions contractors or persons acting on the Company's behalf; the grant runs only to the Company and (now) its affiliates.

Section 1.4 grants access to HDI's hosted system and tools for the hosting relationship; no paid-up/fully-paid licence concept appears in the cited text and the fee/term provisions are not before us, so it cannot be determined whether the condition applies or is satisfied.
No paid-up licence is identified in the rendered language and no irrevocability wording was added; the payment/term provisions are outside the cited excerpt.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The termination provisions of the hosting agreement are not in the rendered excerpt, and no language limiting revocation/termination of the Section 1.4 rights to uncured material breach was added.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.3: the Agreement "shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns", so the Section 1.4 rights pass to and are enforceable by Company successors.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: The added sentence extends the Section 1.4 access and use rights to "the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI" — exactly the notice-conditioned affiliate coverage the fallback requires.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3 (unamended) makes the Agreement enforceable by and for the benefit of the parties' "successors and assigns" without any consent gate on Company transfers, covering an M&A successor.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice is added by a single operative sentence in Section 1.4, and successor transferability is already delivered by retained Section 10.3, which the redline leaves untouched.

Preferred level is not complete: contractors acting on our behalf are still excluded from the grant, and nothing addresses perpetual/irrevocable paid-up rights or limiting revocation of subscription rights to uncured material breach (the relevant fee and termination provisions are not in the cited excerpt, so those elements cannot be resolved on this record).

Minimal: one concise insertion, no deletions, no paraphrase of surrounding text, no duplicated operative terms ("Company" is defined as The Deerskin Companies, Inc. only, so affiliates were genuinely uncovered), and no extras such as survival tails, sublicensing, or contractor language beyond the chosen fallback checklist. No separate personnel/access edit was added, correctly, since nothing retained contradicts the new affiliate grant.

Intent preserved: the bandwidth, capacity, and catalog-monitoring purpose language in Section 1.4 survives intact; Section 10.3 and its "no other person shall acquire rights" limitation are unchanged; no cross-reference is left dangling. Minor drafting note only (not a deviation): "affiliates" is used in lower case and is undefined in the Agreement — consider "affiliates (entities controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the Company)" if HDI raises scope.

Classification as deviation is supportable: without the insertion the fallback failed on affiliate coverage; the grant is not expressly revocable at HDI's discretion, so this is not walk-away territory.
